extracted.intended_audience: readers, potential subscribers, contributors and advertisers of The Forerunner (Charlotte Perkins Gilman)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial/contribution and advertising guidelines for The Forerunner magazine (Charlotte Perkins Gilman): what the magazine publishes, its purposes and values, and rules for advertising and the Personal Problems department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a monthly magazine, publishing stories short and serial, article and essay; drama, verse, satire and sermon; dialogue, fable and fantasy, comment and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Forerunner will include a wide variety of literary forms in each issue (serial novel, short stories, essays, drama, verse, satire, sermons, dialogues, fables, fantasies, comments, reviews). Contributions should fit one of these forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-author policy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is written entirely by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine's content is produced solely by C. P. Gilman, which implies a unified authorial voice and that the publisher does not accept third-party editorial content for the main pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial mission / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: It is to stimulate thought: to arouse hope, courage and impatience; to offer practical suggestions and solutions, to voice the strong assurance of better living, here, now, in our own hands to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should aim to provoke thought and action, offer practical solutions, and present an optimistic, reform-minded view of improving everyday life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: It is about people, principles, and the questions of every-day life; the personal and public problems of to-day. It gives a clear, consistent view of human life and how to live it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer pieces that treat concrete human concerns—personal and public problems—framed with principles and practical guidance for living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to gender and subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: It will treat all three phases of our existence--male, female and human. It will discuss Man, in his true place in life; Woman, the Unknown Power; the Child, the most important citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should address men, women, and children, with particular attention to the condition and potential of women and children as citizens; avoid one-sided or purely gender-stereotyped treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological stance
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a magazine for humanity, and humanity is social. It holds that Socialism, the economic theory, is part of our gradual Socialization, and that the duty of conscious humanity is to promote Socialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine embraces socialization/socialist-leaning perspectives; contributions sympathetic to social reform and socialistic analysis are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising honesty and endorsement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In its advertising department, under the above heading, will be described articles personally known and used. So far as individual experience and approval carry weight, and clear truthful description command attention, the advertising pages of The Forerunner will be useful to both dealer and buyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising should be based on personal knowledge and truthful description; ads describing items the editor or endorsers personally use are preferred to purely promotional copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher discretion on advertiser statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If advertisers prefer to use their own statements The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Forerunner will print advertisers' own copy only when the editor judges those statements credible; the publisher exercises editorial vetting of ad claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising as utility to reader and dealer
rubrics_metrics.description: "A pleased customer is the best advertiser." The Forerunner offers to its advertisers and readers the benefit of this authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ads should aim to be genuinely useful and informative to readers, relying on customer satisfaction and truthful description rather than deceptive rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Problems department scope and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of "Personal Problems" does not discuss etiquette, fashions or the removal of freckles. Foolish questions will not be answered, unless at peril of the asker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Personal Problems column will address serious personal and social issues, not trivial matters of etiquette or fashion; frivolous or 'foolish' queries will be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned regular contents and promised value to subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take this magazine one year you will have: One complete novel . . . By C. P. Gilman; One new book . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve short stories . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve-and-more short articles . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve-and-more new poems . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve Short Sermons . . . By C. P. Gilman; Besides 'Comment and Review' . . . By C. P. Gilman; 'Personal Problems' . . . By C. P. Gilman; And many other things . . . By C. P. Gilman
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher sets clear subscriber expectations about regular serialized and recurring content (novel, book, stories, articles, poems, sermons, reviews, personal problems column) and price ($1.00 a year, .10 a copy). Material and marketing should align with these promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising/rental listing disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The people who own [the cottage] will answer further questions and state facts fully on request, both advantages and disadvantages. The list of furnishings is accurate and circumstantial, as follows: [inventory].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified/rental ads should provide accurate, circumstantial inventories and be willing to disclose both advantages and disadvantages on request; full factual disclosure is required.
